extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings (respondents, OED, administrative counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for appealing an Administrative Law Judge's initial decision in USPTO enrollment and discipline matters under 37 C.F.R. § 10.155 (including timing, content, service, and consequences of failure to comply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of appeal (30-day limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal must be filed within thirty (30) days from the date of the initial decision of the administrative law judge (37 C.F.R. § 10.155(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thirty-day time limit is strict; the deadline expired at midnight on the 30th day. An appeal that is late (including attempted supplementation after the 30-day window) is untimely and will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal must include exceptions and supporting reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent's appeal must 'include exceptions to the decisions of the administrative law judge and supporting reasons for those exceptions' (37 C.F.R. § 10.155(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bare notice of appeal (e.g., a single-sentence appeal without stated exceptions or reasons) fails to satisfy the regulatory requirement. The requirement serves the public interest in prompt resolution of disciplinary matters; appeals lacking exceptions with reasons are deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reply to a reply brief permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision under 37 C.F.R. § 10.155(a) allowing a respondent to file a 'reply to the reply brief' filed by the Director/other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the other party (e.g., OED Director) files a reply brief, the rules do not authorize further responsive filings by the respondent; such filings are improper and may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record completion upon Director's reply; supplementation not allowed after reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 10.155(a), the record is deemed complete as of the filing of the Director's reply; filings purportedly supplementing the appeal after that point are improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent files additional material after the Director's reply (or after the 30-day appeal window), that material will not be considered as part of the appeal record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to appeal under § 10.155 deemed acceptance and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of an appeal by the respondent under the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 10.155, the respondent's failure to appeal is deemed both acceptance by the respondent of the initial decision and waiver of the right to further administrative or judicial review (37 C.F.R. § 10.155(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deficient or absent appeal has the substantive consequence of finalizing the ALJ decision and forfeiting further review rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other party may file a reply brief (timing of reply)
rubrics_metrics.description: The other party to an appeal (e.g., the Director) may file a reply brief. The time for filing any reply brief expires thirty (30) days after the date of service of an appeal (37 C.F.R. § 10.155(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing and service timetable governs when the record is transmitted and when the respondent may (or may not) respond further; service must be effected consistent with the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director must transmit entire record to Commissioner upon filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the filing of an appeal, cross-appeal, and any reply briefs, the Director shall transmit the entire record to the Commissioner (37 C.F.R. § 10.155(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission of the full administrative record occurs once the appeal/reply cycle (as allowed by the regulation) is complete; incomplete or defective appeals may result in the Director transmitting a record that reflects the deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final agency action timing under § 10.156
rubrics_metrics.description: An order by the Commissioner becomes final agency action twenty (20) days after entry, subject to 37 C.F.R. § 10.156(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision will become final after the 20-day period unless the conditions of § 10.156(c) alter that timing; practitioners should note this deadline for any further steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and service requirements (certificate of service, proof of mailing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing practices include service on the opposing party and certificates of service (e.g., a certificate indicating mailing date); the regulation contemplates service and filing mechanics tied to timing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document dates (service date, mailing date) affect timeliness calculations. For example, a certificate showing a mailing date may be used to establish when a document was served/filed for purposes of the 30-day limit and reply deadlines.
